More often, it persists because ordinary things continue performing functions that no longer require an audience.

turns.excerpt: Excerpt 2 — Maps Drawn After the Flood Cartographers rarely admit how much uncertainty exists beneath a finished map. Every line suggests confidence, even when the landscape itself refuses consistency. Rivers migrate, shorelines retreat, and roads gradually become stories told by older residents rather than routes anyone still follows. Accuracy therefore becomes less a property of the document than of its relationship with time. A perfect map is simply one whose inaccuracies have not yet become visible. Eventually every representation gives way, not because it was careless, but because the world continues negotiating its own outline.

turns.excerpt: Excerpt 3 — The Quiet Mechanics of Conversation People often imagine conversations as exchanges of information, although very little information actually changes hands. More commonly, each remark adjusts the conditions under which the next remark becomes possible. Agreement is built gradually, hesitation acquires meaning through repetition, and silence occasionally performs more work than explanation. This is why misunderstandings rarely begin with dramatic errors. They usually emerge from small assumptions that remain unexamined because every subsequent sentence quietly accepts them. By the time disagreement becomes visible, its foundations have already settled beyond immediate correction.
